sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r3/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: Quality Checks row 25 and Internal Quality Checks row 25 (judge_prompts_drive_the_browser; no extra annotation/comment on the row; drawings empty)
evidence: All five dimension prompts open the live app and name the browser tool on line 1: gates/render/prompt.md:1, gates/constraints/prompt.md:1, scored/functional/prompt.md:1, scored/polish/prompt.md:1 ('Evaluate the live application at http://localhost:3000 using Playwright MCP.') and scored/visual/prompt.md:1-2 ('Evaluate the rendered application at http://localhost:3000 using Playwright MCP.'), identical to the frozen template's opening. Every judge.toml wires the browser: [[judge.mcp_servers]] name=playwright, command=playwright-mcp, args --headless --isolated --executable-path=/usr/local/bin/chromium (render/constraints/polish/visual judge.toml:11-15, functional judge.toml:16-20; functional also has the verifier restart server at 23-27); tests/Dockerfile:19,33-38 installs @playwright/mcp@0.0.79 and links chromium. Source/memory/first-paint scoring is excluded in text: render prompt.md:2 'Use only rendered browser behavior'; constraints prompt.md:2 'browser-visible behavior and browser network evidence only' and :10-12 'A blank page... is not proof of a constraint'; functional prompt.md:24-28 'passes only on evidence you gathered in this session... never pass a criterion on a general impression', :36-41 'use rendered controls... Never use curl or shell commands', :48 'Never ... run shell or install commands'; polish prompt.md:4 'Judge the rendered product and interactions, not code style' and :22 'from browser-visible evidence'; visual prompt.md:40 'from rendered evidence'. All three scored prompts restate the in-dimension gate including 'a first-paint imitation does not pass' (functional 11-19, polish 10-18, visual 18-26). All prompts treat 'source' as untrusted evidence (line 2-4 each). Criteria are interactive, not first-paint: render gate signs in, rejects wrong password (render judge.toml:26-30); constraints gate posts 'Gate check JUDGE-G1', reloads and reads it from a second context as harriet (constraints judge.toml:26-36); functional criteria record and replay in-page requests and use restart_app; polish phone_matter/visual phone_chambers resize to 390x844 and visual prompt.md:49 orders resize to 1440x900; polish refusal_in_place waits ~10 s. No prompt or criterion cites source files, server.js, app.db or SQLite (grep of tests/*/*/judge.toml, prompt.md, app_context.md). Placeholders resolve: every prompt carries {app_context} and {criteria}; test.sh:195-201 substitutes {app_context} into /tests/*/*/prompt.md covering both gates/* and scored/*. In functional individual mode (judge.toml:6) each per-criterion session receives the same full prompt, so the browser directive is repeated per session. app_context.md:4,24-26 repeat URL localhost:3000 and explain how to open a second Playwright context. Counterexample search: (a) broken app that could pass - a static/hard-coded shell or localStorage-only chat: the constraints gate requires a posted message to survive reload and appear in a separate harriet context, and scored gates reject 'static shell... seeded-looking facade'; a judge reading /app source instead (isolated=false, /app is a+rX per test.sh:85) is forbidden by the browser-only and no-shell wording, so no prompt can be satisfied by reading source. (b) conforming alternative that could fail - an app with different routes, cookie names or labels: prompts say 'Do not guess URL paths', 'Any endpoint path, payload shape or cookie name is acceptable', 'Match controls by intent and label' and the brief mandates port 3000 (integration.md:3), so the browser directive imposes no hidden requirement. No defect found for this row. Limit: this is a source review. raw-evidence-index.json scope states full configured grading is absent; the cited scripted golden run (Playwright scripts, not the claude-code/GLM judge) does not show whether the configured judge actually invokes the Playwright MCP tool rather than its own shell tools. That runtime behaviour belongs to the full-verifier-launch evidence rows; it does not change the prompt-content verdict here.
